title: quantization-performance-benchmarks-int8-gptq-awq
summary: Internal benchmark note summarizing INT8 / FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ quantization quality vs performance tradeoffs across kernels and hardware. Includes methodology, dataset, metric definitions, key results and next steps for kernel integration and auto-selection heuristics.
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an initial set of experiments to quantify the performance and quality tradeoffs for common quantization schemes we plan to support in the serving runtime: INT8 (per-channel and per-tensor), FP8 (E4M3/E5M2 variants), GPTQ (batch & layerwise variants), and AWQ. The goal is to provide actionable data for: (1) kernel selection and default runtime policy, (2) auto-quantization recommendations in Redwood Optimize, and (3) fallback/rollout policies for low-quality regressions.

Scope and constraints:
- Models tested: MPT-7B (7B decoder), LLaMA-2-7B, and a 13B internal variant used in customer trials.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 (40GB), NVIDIA H100 (80GB), and an INT8-optimized edge GPU (NVIDIA T4) for cost-sensitivity checks.
- Serving config: single-model pinned instance; sequence lengths: 128 and 2048; batch sizes: 1, 4, 16 (where memory allowed).
- Kernels: reference float32 GEMM path, cuBLAS/FlashAttention variants, fused QKV kernels, and our quantized GEMM kernels (QGEMM-perchannel, QGEMM-quantize-on-load).
- Evaluation metrics: throughput (tokens/s), latency P50/P95/P99 (ms per request), memory footprint (GPU memory), and quality: perplexity on held-out LM eval set + task-specific exact-match/F1 on a small QA prompt set and average log-prob delta relative to fp16 baseline.
- Profiling tools: Nsight Systems for timeline + kernel breakdown, nvprof/cupti counters for FLOPs and memory bandwidth when needed, and our internal token-level tracer to measure KV cache effects.

Methodology:
1) Convert model variants using standard recipes: GPTQ (bitsandbytes-style rounding) and AWQ binaries where applicable. For INT8 we tried both per-tensor symmetric quant and per-channel asymmetric quant. For FP8 we tested E4M3 and E5M2 encodings using the available conversion toolchain.
2) Run warmup of 200 requests to saturate kernels and allow caching behaviors to stabilize.
3) Measure steady-state throughput and latency distributed over 30s windows. Capture kernel-level breakdown via Nsight.
4) Run quality checks: LM perplexity on WikiText subset (2k tokens) and a 200-prompt QA suite representative of customer prompt patterns (structured prompts with code, JSON, and long contexts). Compute relative perplexity delta and task accuracy.
5) Repeat for sequence lengths = {128, 2048} and batch sizes = {1,4,16} when memory allows.

Key observations (high-level):
- INT8 (per-channel) paired with optimized QGEMM kernels gives the best latency and throughput gains across all GPUs at batch sizes 1 and 4. Typical speedups vs fp16: 1.6x-2.3x throughput; median p50 latency drop 30-55% depending on model and kernel. Quality delta is small for many layers but non-negligible on LLaMA-2-7B: perplexity increased 4-7% on average and some prompt-specific hallucination patterns were observed.
- GPTQ yields large model-size reductions and steady inference speedups (1.8x-2.5x), but quality varies by model and tuning recipe. GPTQ-converted checkpoints showed a mean perplexity increase of 3-6% on MPT and 6-10% on LLaMA-2-7B depending on quantization bits. GPTQ tends to introduce structured degradation on long-context tasks (2048) unless dequantization hacks are applied for attention kernels.
- AWQ consistently produced lower quality degradation compared to vanilla GPTQ at the same effective bit-width for our tested models (typical perplexity delta: 1-4%). AWQ's inference speed is close to GPTQ but required specific kernel paths to exploit its packing layout; without the optimized kernels AWQ runs slower than INT8 QGEMM.
- FP8 (E4M3) shows a middle-ground: lower memory footprint than fp16 and better quality than 8-bit integer in some layers (notably softmax & norm-sensitive layers). Throughput gains are modest unless combined with FP8-optimized GEMM kernels and compiler support (1.2x-1.6x). On H100, FP8 was particularly effective when using the hardware FP8 instructions (significant reduction in dequant overhead).
- Kernel selection matters: a naive cuBLAS path on quantized weights often defeats the expected perf wins due to conversion overheads. Fused quantized GEMM + fused attention kernels with pre-packed weights are essential to get the full benefit. Our QGEMM-perchannel + fused KV cache path provided the best latency for batch=1 across A100/H100.

Representative numbers (MPT-7B, seq_len=128, batch=1):
- fp16 baseline: throughput 650 tokens/s, p50 18ms, GPU mem 12GB, perplexity 18.3
- INT8 (per-channel, QGEMM fused): throughput 1250 tokens/s, p50 9ms, GPU mem 9GB, perplexity 19.1 (+4.4%)
- GPTQ (8-bit, optimized): throughput 1350 tokens/s, p50 8.6ms, GPU mem 6.5GB, perplexity 19.8 (+8.2%)
- AWQ (8-bit, optimized kernels): throughput 1280 tokens/s, p50 9.2ms, GPU mem 7GB, perplexity 18.8 (+2.7%)
- FP8 (E4M3, hw-accel on H100): throughput 780 tokens/s, p50 15ms, GPU mem 8.5GB, perplexity 18.6 (+1.6%)

Representative numbers (LLaMA-2-7B, seq_len=2048, batch=1):
- fp16 baseline: throughput 120 tokens/s, p50 120ms, perplexity 12.9
- INT8 (per-channel): throughput 220 tokens/s, p50 68ms, perplexity 14.2 (+10.1%)
- GPTQ: throughput 240 tokens/s, p50 62ms, perplexity 15.0 (+16.3%)
- AWQ: throughput 230 tokens/s, p50 64ms, perplexity 13.6 (+5.4%)
- FP8: not stable for 2048 without extra numerics tuning on LLaMA-2-7B (we aborted runs due to outlier token probabilities causing QA failures)

Profiling notes (kernel-level):
- For INT8 runs on A100, the dominant kernels were QGEMM (45-60% timeline), then fused attention (25-35%), with memory copies making up remaining overhead. Pre-packing weights during model load reduces steady-state QGEMM overhead by ~20% compared to quantize-on-the-fly.
- GPTQ binaries benefited from smaller memory traffic but displayed more scattered small kernels that increased p99 latency due to less efficient kernel packing.
- AWQ requires custom packing of weight blocks; our prototype kernel that reads AWQ-block layout had ~10% more instruction-level efficiency than generic GPTQ unpacking, translating to slightly lower p99.

Quality failure modes and mitigation:
- Token-level spikes: observed for INT8/per-tensor in certain normalization layers leading to high-prob tokens mid-generation. Mitigation: prefer per-channel quantization for layers with high dynamic range (LayerNorm, final projection).
- Long-context drift: GPTQ sometimes amplifies context drift in 2k+ sequences. Mitigation: selective re-quantization of attention projection layers at higher precision, or hybrid models where attention/LayerNorm kept at fp16.
- FP8 instability on some LLaMA variants: required numerics clamping and bias-correction during quantize pipeline.

Recommendations for runtime defaults (interim):
1) Default profile for hosted-api and dedicated: INT8 per-channel with pre-packed QGEMM + fused-attention kernels for batch sizes <=4 where supported. Provide fp16 fallback and an "allow-higher-precision-attention" flag to keep attention & norms as fp16 when customers enable stricter quality SLAs.
2) AWQ as the preferred GPTQ-like option when customers request aggressive size reduction but want better quality; ensure our kernel packers are available in the runtime.
3) Expose an auto-eval step on model upload (QuickQualityCheck): run a small set of prompts to estimate perplexity delta and if above threshold (configurable) automatically pin a hybrid quantization policy (e.g., keep attention layers at fp16).
4) Model crops & sequence-length-aware kernel selection: for long-context workloads favor fp16 or FP8 on H100 with hardware fp8 accel; for short interactive prompts prefer INT8 optimized kernels.

Next steps / action items:
- (Eng) Flesh out QGEMM-perchannel production kernel with pre-pack stage and test on H100 microbenchmarks. Owner: Mateo Chavez. ETA: 2026-03-05.
- (Perf) Run broader sweep across our internal 13B customer model set and produce aggregated quality-cost curves. Owner: Lin Wei. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- (Product) Design "QuickQualityCheck" UX and thresholds; integrate with model upload pipeline (Optimize feature). Owner: Priya Kapoor. ETA: 2026-03-12.
- (SRE) Add perf guardrails in Dedicated rollout: reject quantized image if QuickQualityCheck fails or p99 latency worsens >2x on canary machines. Owner: SRE team. ETA: 2026-03-18.

Notes / open questions:
- Need to confirm licensing/redistribution constraints for AWQ tooling and ensure compatibility with our on-prem packaging.
- Evaluate cost/benefit of adding FP8 hardware-specific paths only for H100 vs attempting a portable emulation path for A100.
- Determine the auto-selection policy granularity: model-level only, or layer-level hybrid quantization made available to customers?

Appendix: short checklist for repeatability:
- Use identical random seed for conversion pipelines where supported.
- Persist packed weight artifacts and record pack version + kernel version in metadata.
- Include Nsight system traces, perf counters, and the QuickQualityCheck output as linked artifacts for each run.

-- end of note --
